The paper operates at a frequency of 10 GHz for all simulations.
The ground-based SAR system uses a 10-meter rail length for antenna movement.
The radar antenna height in the experimental model is 30 meters.
The off-nadir angle used in the SAR geometry is 45 degrees.
All canonical targets (flat plate, dihedral, trihedral) have dimensions of 1m × 1m.
The flat plate shows a maximum co-polarized RCS of -19.58 dBsm in HH polarization.
The flat plate shows a maximum cross-polarized RCS of -337.4 dBsm in VH polarization.
The dihedral reflector achieves higher RCS values than the flat plate across all polarizations.
The trihedral reflector shows the highest co-polarized RCS values among the three targets at -12.54 dBsm (HH).
Co-polarized RCS values are consistently 50-300 dB higher than cross-polarized values.
The scattering matrix has four components: S_hh, S_hv, S_vh, and S_vv.
Physical optics approximation assumes perfectly conducting surfaces.
The dihedral reflector involves up to three levels of reflections between two perpendicular plates.
The trihedral reflector involves 24 different reflection path combinations.
The paper uses both Physical Optics (PO) and Geometrical Optics (GO) methods for different reflection calculations.
RCS measurements are expressed in dBsm (decibels relative to one square meter).
The scattered electric field components in spherical coordinates include radial (E_r), theta (E_θ), and phi (E_φ) components.
The paper demonstrates that RCS peaks when the SAR is closest to the scattering target.
Cross-polarized returns are sensitive to surface roughness and complex scattering mechanisms.
The wavenumber k relates to frequency through k = 2πf/c.
The impedance of free space (η) is used in calculating far-field scattered electric field components.
SAR geometry causes continuous changes in incident and scattered field angles during observation.
The paper confirms that simulation results conform with standard electromagnetic theory.
Horizontal polarization is represented by the y-component of scattered electric field.
Vertical polarization is represented by the z-component of scattered electric field.
